Hi Aditya / Monica,

We noticed a sudden jump in Metering records reported through AWS Marketplace for our tenant between 2027-04-25 02:00 UTC and 2027-04-27 05:00 UTC. Our finance team just received Invoice #0427 and the total is ~3.8x our normal month — we believe this is incorrect.

I've attached the invoice PDF and a CSV export from our side (acme_usage_export_20270427.csv) showing the consumer-side events. The spike correlates with a background job started by a new integration last Friday, but the event shapes don't match our expected consumption pattern.

Can you confirm whether Redwood's metering connector sent duplicate usage lines or if AWS Marketplace reported duplicate ticks? We need a quick triage and a plan for either a post-bill credit or a correction before the payment is processed.

Thanks,
Rajiv Sharma
Head of Billing Operations
Acme Analytics

Hi all — I pulled the metering ingest logs for tenant acme-prod. Summary from initial pass:

- Between 2027-04-25T02:03:12Z and 2027-04-27T05:01:08Z we recorded a series of metering events with three distinct outer IDs that match the consumer_ids in Acme's CSV. The events were generated by our runtime's async batching worker.
- Ingest logs show a retry storm on Apr 25 at 02:03 UTC originating from a downstream error code (HTTP 5xx) when writing to the Marketplace fulfillment endpoint; our client retried with exponential backoff and may have resubmitted some batched records rather than the dedup-safe single-record token.

What I need from AWS Marketplace team (Sara): can you provide the Marketplace receipt logs for case CASE-987654 (linked above) for those timestamps and confirm whether Marketplace accepted duplicate lines as independent consumption or applied deduplication? We need to understand whether the extra tokens were billed by Marketplace or were simply recorded in our logs but later collapsed.

Planned immediate steps (our side):
- Export raw metering payloads paired with our internal ingestion IDs (ETA: 12 hours).
- Identify retry batches that overlap with the spike window and mark candidate duplicates.
- Prepare redline for a potential post-bill credit and proposed credit amount (ETA: 48 hours).

Rajiv / Acme: if you can also share the CloudTrail event IDs for the integration job (integration-job-qa-7832) and the specific consumer_id list, that will speed mapping.

Karthik Iyer
Marketplace Operations Lead, Redwood Inference

Hi Rajiv / Sara / team — quick status update and proposed next steps.

1) Investigation results:
- Redwood identified ~9,800 candidate duplicate metering lines emitted by our async batching worker during the retry window. These appear to be the primary driver of the billed delta.
- We correlated those candidate duplicates to Acme's consumer_id list (A-9923) and attached the candidate list to the HubSpot ticket.
- AWS Marketplace has confirmed (Sara, thanks) that the Marketplace accepted each submitted record as distinct consumption because the incoming payloads lacked the deduplication token we recommend.

2) Remediation plan:
- Redwood will propose a post-bill credit equal to the gross cost of the candidate duplicate units (~$18,400).
- We'll issue an internal refund/credit note and submit the supporting reconciliation to AWS Marketplace for their records.
- To prevent recurrence: implement stricter dedup token propagation in our batching worker (deploy target: 2027-05-07) and add an ingestion alert when retry volume exceeds threshold.

3) Timeline and asks:
- Redwood to provide a formal credit memo draft by 2027-05-02.
- Acme to confirm acceptance of the credit proposal and preferred handling (apply to next invoice vs. one-time refund) by 2027-05-04.
- We'll keep the HubSpot ticket updated: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/ACME-12345

Thank you for patience — we realize this impacts your finance close and will prioritize a clean resolution.

Best,
Monica Patel
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
